index.title: Project overview
index.heading: Product entity matching with RoBERTa and comparison features
index.lead: Compare retailer listings using their text and product fields. The model combines a joint text representation with explicit comparisons of titles, model numbers, brands and prices, and returns a score for each pair.
index.description: Product-pair input, field preparation, RoBERTa feature fusion and results on a fixed retrospective evaluation pool.

method.title: Data & method
method.heading: Data preparation and RoBERTa feature fusion
method.lead: Normalization creates consistent views of product fields. A 42-dimensional comparison vector records agreement, differences and missing values; RoBERTa encodes both listing orders. Development and calibration data select the checkpoint and decision cutoff.
method.description: Six stages covering inputs, normalization, roles, 42 comparisons, RoBERTa fusion, score aggregation and calibration.

results.title: Results
results.heading: Retrospective results on [[evaluation]] product pairs
results.lead: Compare six methods on the same product pairs: four models based on numerical comparisons, the final text-and-feature model C+, and the independently trained C0 control whose comparison features are set to zero. AP measures ranking; F1 measures decisions at each method’s calibration cutoff.
results.description: Six-method aggregate comparison, calibrated C+ confusion counts and limits of the fixed retrospective evaluation.

overview_example_title: Field normalization and eight example comparisons
example_note: The compact forms of ZX-100 and ZX100 agree, while ZX-101 has different digits. This illustrates two operations in the feature pipeline: compare formatting variants, and record model-code disagreements. The listings are synthetic; neither has been scored by RoBERTa, and their identity is not a measured result.
overview_result_title: C+ results on the fixed evaluation pool
p100_expansion: Precision among the first 100 ranked pairs
overview_result_note: C+ averages the probabilities from three training seeds. On the [[evaluation]] fixed Walmart–Amazon pairs, it reached AP [[ap4]], F1 [[f14]] and P@100 [[p100]]. Against L42, the best tabular reference on this pool, AP was [[delta_ap]] percentage points higher and F1 was [[delta_f1]] percentage points higher. The AP difference from C0 was only [[delta_c0_ap]] percentage points, so the comparison does not establish a substantial ranking gain from the feature input.
scope: The evaluation is retrospective. The fixed pool’s historical exposure record is incomplete, and performance on an independent new Walmart–Amazon sample has not been tested.
overview_choice_title: Six-stage data preparation and scoring procedure
fields_p: The input has title, brand, description, price and currency fields, plus native model number and category fields. Text is normalized for comparison, and missing or ambiguous values retain explicit states. Prices are compared only when both values parse and their recognized currencies agree. Separate model-code comparisons record matching codes, edit distance and disagreements in letters or digits.
model_title: Direction averaging and three-seed probability ensemble
model_p: Within each seed, the same trained model scores AB and BA order. Compute p_seed = sigmoid((logit_AB + logit_BA) / 2), then take the equal mean of the probabilities from seeds [[seeds]], using the common checkpoint at epoch [[epoch]]. This produces one continuous C+ score; the calibration cutoff is applied afterwards. Averaging logits before sigmoid and averaging seed probabilities afterwards are distinct operations, and this order is preserved.
overview_close_title: Public files and local artifact requirements
overview_close_p: The repository includes model source, fixed settings, six-method aggregate results, bilingual guides and executable examples. Start with the environment and quickstart instructions to check the code and preview this website. Real model prediction additionally requires locally supplied product inputs, model snapshots and trained weights.
roles_title: Fit, development, calibration and evaluation roles
roles_intro: The pairs have four preassigned project roles. Fit is used to estimate model parameters and title IDF; development selects an epoch; calibration selects a cutoff; evaluation supplies the reported comparison. These assignments do not establish an untouched official test split or an entity-disjoint evaluation.
role_p: Fit title IDF, the tabular references and each neural training seed.
Use the three seeds’ development predictions to select one common epoch.
Use calibration scores and labels to select a cutoff by F1, then precision, then the higher cutoff.
Apply the saved cutoff and report ranking metrics and integer prediction counts.
roles_note: Only fit model inputs contain target labels. Development, calibration and evaluation labels are held in separate files and joined to scores by pair_id for their respective commands. Non-fit preparation reuses the saved fit IDF state. These input rules describe the current code; they cannot reconstruct the fixed pool’s incomplete historical exposure record.
processing_title: Field normalization, quality states and title IDF
processing_names: Title IDF fitted on fit records
processing_p: Text comparison uses Unicode normalization, case folding and whitespace cleanup. Missing brand, description, model and category values remain missing; the feature vector records presence indicators where defined. Two absent values are not counted as a positive equality comparison.

A plain nonnegative decimal can be parsed as a price. Ambiguous symbols or separators keep an unresolved quality state. Price similarity is enabled only when both prices parse and their recognized currency codes agree; otherwise the comparable-price indicator is zero. No exchange-rate conversion or price imputation is applied.

Model-like title codes are extracted and compared as sets. Features describe exact overlap, normalized edit similarity and shared letters with different digits or shared digits with different letters. Native model numbers are compared separately and checked against the opposite listing’s title codes.

Title word and character document frequencies are fitted on content-deduplicated business records from fit only. The saved IDF state weights title overlap in later roles without refitting. Direct title-number and compact-title comparisons are also included; they do not require fitting. For example, in 100 synthetic training records, a term appearing in 80 of those records has weight 1 + ln(101/81) ≈ 1.221; one appearing in two records has weight 1 + ln(101/3) ≈ 4.517. Common terms therefore contribute less evidence of overlap. These counts illustrate the calculation; they are not dataset statistics.
features_intro: Preparation produces one x42 vector per pair. Its four groups have 14, 8, 8 and 12 values, in the exact order recorded in FEATURES.json. IDs and labels are excluded. Similarity values for missing inputs are zero, with separate presence or comparability indicators where defined. Expand a group to inspect its identifiers and descriptions.
feature_group_names: Title IDF and direct title comparisons
feature_group_p: Fourteen values compare title and description tokens, brand agreement, numeric tokens, title length and prices. Presence and price-comparability indicators distinguish unavailable evidence from a measured similarity.

Eight values contain four IDF-weighted title similarities and four direct comparisons of mixed alphanumeric tokens, numeric tokens, numeric presence and compact-title equality. Only the IDF state is fitted, using fit records.
Eight values compare model-like codes extracted from titles. They cover missingness, exact overlap, set overlap, best edit similarity and differences in the letter and digit parts.
Twelve values compare native model numbers and categories, including presence, equality, edit/trigram similarity and whether a native model appears in the other listing’s title codes.
architecture_title: RoBERTa text encoding and feature-fusion head
architecture_intro: Each seed uses the same architecture with its own trained parameters. The text branch receives brand, native model number, category and title. The comparison branch supplies x42, including description and price evidence. The fusion head returns one logit for each listing order; aggregation produces the final pair score.
diagram_title: C+ inputs, fusion head and score aggregation
diagram_description: Two product listings enter AB and BA encodings. RoBERTa CLS is projected to 64 units and joined with [[features]] comparison features. A fusion head gives logits. Average AB and BA logits, apply sigmoid, then average seed probabilities.
architecture_note: For each AB or BA input, the 768-dimensional RoBERTa first-token representation passes through a 64-unit GELU projection. Concatenating [[features]] comparisons gives 106 inputs to a second 64-unit GELU layer; dropout [[dropout]] and a linear layer produce one logit. Average AB and BA logits, apply sigmoid, then take the equal probability mean over seeds [[seeds]]. Each pair is limited to 256 tokens. Field budgets are brand 16, model 32, category 16 and title 62; a long title retains the first 40 and last 22 tokens.
configuration_title: Fixed training settings and selected checkpoint
configuration_intro: C+ trains with a six-epoch schedule. Development compares ensemble predictions and selected common epoch [[epoch]] for seeds [[seeds]]. Calibration selected cutoff [[threshold]], which evaluation reuses. The table records the frozen settings; it is not a new tuning or training run.
precision_training: BF16 encoder; FP32 parameters and head
method_scope: This page describes the fixed implementation. New-source generalization and a fresh end-to-end training reproduction remain unverified.
comparison_title: AP ranking and F1 at calibrated cutoffs
comparison_intro: All six methods scored the same [[evaluation]]-pair retrospective pool, including [[positive]] matches. Each method uses its own calibration cutoff for F1. AP compares ranking without that cutoff. Both plot axes cover 0–1, and the table keeps six decimal places.
chart_f1_title: F1 at each method’s calibration cutoff
chart_caption: C+ is the final three-seed ensemble. C0 is trained independently, with all 42 comparison values zeroed in both training and inference. B22, L30, S33 and L42 are the four tabular references.
nojs: Both complete plots remain visible when JavaScript is disabled.

methods.S33: L30 plus three MiniLM semantic/missingness features
methods.C0: Independently trained RoBERTa control with x42 zeroed

table_caption: AP and F1 are distinct measures. The CSV contains the original unrounded metric values, integer counts and each calibration cutoff.
matrix_title: C+ confusion matrix at the calibration cutoff
matrix_caption: Rows are actual classes; columns are predictions. [[evaluation]] pairs in total, with [[positive]] actual matches.
matrix_note: At the calibration cutoff [[threshold]], C+ classified [[fp]] nonmatches as matches and missed [[fn]] actual matches. These counts give precision [[precision4]] and recall [[recall4]]. They describe this pair pool. A score alone is insufficient evidence for an automatic catalog merge.
delta_title: C+ differences from L42 and C0
delta_p: Relative to L42 on this pool, C+ AP was [[delta_ap]] percentage points higher and F1 was [[delta_f1]] percentage points higher. Relative to C0, AP was only [[delta_c0_ap]] percentage points higher. C0 is an independently trained control: all 42 feature values are zero during training and inference. It uses the six-epoch scheduler for four training epochs and is compared at epoch 4. The aggregate results do not establish a substantial feature-driven AP gain or statistical significance.
definition_p: Average precision (AP) summarizes precision over the ranking of positive pairs. It uses the continuous pair scores and groups tied scores. AP [[ap4]] is not a classification accuracy of [[ap4]].

F1 combines precision and recall after turning scores into match/nonmatch predictions at a cutoff. The cutoff is selected on calibration labels and fixed before evaluation. Changing it changes the balance of false matches and missed matches.

P@100 is the fraction of actual matches among the first 100 ranked pairs. Score ties at the boundary are ordered by pair_id. P@100 [[p100]] describes those 100 pairs in this pool, rather than all products or future listings.
limits_p: The [[evaluation]]-pair pool is retrospective, and its history of use is not fully documented. No independent new Walmart–Amazon sample or entity-disjoint evaluation is established here. The saved aggregates provide no confidence interval or production latency/business-benefit measurement. Agreement in existing-weight replay verifies artifact preparation and prediction through the public code entry; it does not provide new unseen-data evidence.
public_title: Check the public code and saved outputs
public_intro: After setting up the environment above, run these checks from the repository root. They exercise input interfaces, feature calculations and metric arithmetic using synthetic records, and check the stored aggregate results. They require no model download or GPU.
check_step_title: Interfaces, saved outputs and file checks
check_step_p: public_smoke.py checks the package and CLI entry points. run_notebook.py runs the English and Chinese executable walkthroughs and compares their saved outputs. verify_public_release.py checks the public file inventory, hashes, local links and result arithmetic. A passed report confirms these code and document checks; it does not run model inference.
tests_step_title: CLI help and synthetic contract tests
tests_step_p: The help command shows the explicit preparation, training and prediction entry points. The test suite checks synthetic cases. Passing these tests is separate from reproducing the model experiment.
replay_intro: The public code entry ran [[replay_commands]] commands with original frozen inputs and local model artifacts. [[replay_groups]] independently checked result groups matched the saved outputs; the maximum prediction difference was [[max_difference]]. The replay covered input preparation and existing-model predictions. It did not fit new weights or evaluate an independent new Walmart–Amazon sample.
replay_items: Prepared tokens, 42 features and the fit-only IDF state
Fixed MiniLM semantic features and four reference predictions
Three-seed predictions and final ensemble probabilities
replay_note: Observed environment: Windows 11, Python 3.11.16, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu126 and an RTX 3060 laptop. Other GPU platforms have not been validated. The aggregate record is available as fixed-results.json.
fresh_p: The reconstruct-roles command verifies the original ZIP and restores all four role inputs byte for byte, including the original native missing masks. The recipe contains source positions and hashes, with no product values or labels. GPU replay still requires local snapshots and trusted weights. Fresh end-to-end training and independent new Walmart–Amazon sample evaluation have not been validated.
fresh_note: Use locally supplied artifacts under their applicable terms and a project environment. Fit estimates model parameters and IDF; development selects the epoch; calibration selects the cutoff. Evaluation labels remain separate from model input and are not used to choose these settings. The interface checks do not resolve the historical exposure of the saved evaluation pool.
rebuild_p: The standard-library generator reads the saved aggregate results, final model configuration, feature order and bilingual page text. It writes eight complete HTML pages and a result CSV. This command generates documentation; it neither fetches product data nor loads a model.
rebuild_check_p: The check command generates in memory and compares every generated byte. It does not write files.

data_example_intro: The workbench uses synthetic Acme cordless-drill records and displays normalized fields plus eight selected comparisons from the 42-feature vector. The first scenario changes ZX-100 to ZX100 and brand capitalization while keeping the listing type the same. The second uses ZX101 to expose a model-digit disagreement. The third removes a brand and changes the currency, so presence and price-comparability indicators change.
model_decision_explanation: The final method uses RoBERTa for the paired text and a separate comparison vector for explicit field operations. A title can share many words with another listing while differing in a model digit; a price can be absent or in a different currency. The 42-dimensional comparison vector, named x42 in the code, records those conditions directly. Brand, model, category and title are serialized for RoBERTa, while description and price enter through the feature vector. The 768-dimensional text representation is projected before joining x42. This is the architecture tested in the fixed comparison, not evidence that feature fusion is generally superior: The independently trained C0 control, with all comparison features set to zero, has nearly the same AP on this pool.
reference_comparison_explanation: B22 fits logistic regression on the first 22 comparisons. L30 uses gradient-boosted trees on 30 comparisons; S33 adds three fixed MiniLM semantic/missingness values to that representation. L42 uses all 42 comparisons without RoBERTa, so it supplies the strongest tabular reference measured on this pool. C+ adds paired-text encoding and averages three trained seeds. C0 is trained independently of C+, retains the neural dimensions, and zeros all 42 feature values throughout training and inference. It is evaluated at epoch 4 after four training epochs with the six-epoch scheduler. All six rows use the same evaluation pool; F1 is computed at each method’s calibration cutoff. The comparison is retrospective and does not establish statistical significance.
result_interpretation: Compared with L42, C+ reduces false matches from 35 to 11 while missed matches increase from 23 to 25, improving F1. Its AP is only 0.0381 percentage points above separately trained C0. This comparison does not establish a clear ranking benefit from the 42 features; independent new Walmart–Amazon sample generalization remains untested.

walkthrough_stages.title: Field normalization and quality states
walkthrough_stages.input: Two supplied retailer records with title, brand, description, price and priceCurrency; native modelno and category fields.
walkthrough_stages.operation: Create normalized business and native views. Apply Unicode normalization, case folding and whitespace cleanup to text. Parse plain nonnegative prices, retain missing/ambiguous states, and enable price comparison only for equal recognized currencies.
walkthrough_stages.output: A pair record with pair_id, left, right, left_native and right_native, including explicit price/currency quality states. The original source is not replaced by a guessed value.
walkthrough_stages.rationale: Title formatting varies, while a model digit or currency difference can change what is being compared. Separating normalized values from unavailable evidence prevents missing prices or two absent brands from becoming positive equality evidence.

walkthrough_stages.title: Preassigned data roles and label separation
walkthrough_stages.input: Frozen pair membership and the corresponding fit, dev, calibration and evaluation records; separate non-fit label lists.
walkthrough_stages.operation: Fit model parameters and title IDF on fit. Select one common ensemble epoch on dev. Select a cutoff on calibration. Apply the selected settings to evaluation. Join non-fit labels by pair_id only in the relevant metric or selection command.
walkthrough_stages.output: Prepared role-specific inputs and separate selection/calibration/evaluation labels. The reported evaluation pool has [[evaluation]] pairs, including [[positive]] matches.
walkthrough_stages.rationale: Epoch selection and cutoff selection answer different procedural questions. Keeping them separate prevents the current prediction interface from consuming evaluation labels. It does not establish that the retrospective pool was untouched earlier; its historical exposure record remains incomplete.

walkthrough_stages.title: The [[features]]-dimensional comparison vector
walkthrough_stages.input: Normalized business/native pair views and title IDF fitted on deduplicated fit records.
walkthrough_stages.operation: Compute 14 business comparisons, 8 title-IDF/direct-title comparisons, 8 title-code comparisons and 12 native-model/category comparisons. Preserve the FEATURES.json order and reuse the fit IDF state for later roles.
walkthrough_stages.output: One finite x42 vector in [0, 1] per pair, with similarity, presence, disagreement and comparability values. IDs and target labels are not vector entries.
walkthrough_stages.rationale: The vector gives the model explicit observations such as a shared model code, a changed digit, a missing brand or an incomparable price. The fixed order makes the same meaning available to the tabular references and the neural fusion head.

walkthrough_stages.title: RoBERTa encoding and feature fusion
walkthrough_stages.input: Brand, native model number, category and title serialized in AB and BA order, plus the pair’s x42 vector.
walkthrough_stages.operation: Encode each order with RoBERTa-base within the 256-token limit. Project the 768-dimensional first-token representation to 64 GELU units, concatenate [[features]] comparisons, then apply a 64-unit GELU layer, dropout [[dropout]] and a linear output.
walkthrough_stages.output: One scalar logit for AB and one for BA in each seed. Description and price evidence reach the head through x42, rather than the text serialization.
walkthrough_stages.rationale: The text branch represents the pair’s language, while explicit field comparisons retain model-code and missingness information. This is the tested fusion structure. The near-equal C0 AP limits the feature-contribution conclusion supported by this pool.

walkthrough_stages.title: Direction averaging and three-seed ensemble
walkthrough_stages.input: AB and BA logits from seeds [[seeds]], all using the common checkpoint selected at epoch [[epoch]].
walkthrough_stages.operation: Within each seed, average the two direction logits and apply sigmoid. Then average the three resulting probabilities with equal weights. Direction averaging precedes sigmoid; seed averaging follows it.
walkthrough_stages.output: One continuous C+ score for each pair_id. This score is later ranked or compared with the calibration cutoff.
walkthrough_stages.rationale: Processing both listing orders makes the score symmetric to swapping the inputs. Averaging three fixed seeds defines the reported ensemble without selecting the most favorable seed on evaluation labels.

walkthrough_stages.title: Calibration cutoff and fixed-pool evaluation
walkthrough_stages.input: Calibration scores and labels, followed by evaluation scores and separately supplied evaluation labels.
walkthrough_stages.operation: Choose maximum calibration F1, then precision, then the higher cutoff. Freeze cutoff [[threshold]] for C+. Align evaluation scores and labels by pair_id, compute AP with score ties grouped, P@100 with pair_id tie ordering, and the integer confusion matrix.
walkthrough_stages.output: C+ AP [[ap4]], F1 [[f14]] and P@100 [[p100]] on [[evaluation]] pairs; TP [[tp]], FP [[fp]], FN [[fn]] and TN [[tn]].
walkthrough_stages.rationale: AP measures ranking, while F1 evaluates decisions at the selected cutoff and P@100 describes only the first 100 pairs. These results belong to the fixed retrospective pool. They do not establish independent new Walmart–Amazon sample performance, and replay agreement is not fresh training or a new evaluation.

model_definition: C+ names the final model in this project: RoBERTa with 42 comparison features, averaged across three training seeds.
quickstart_intro: Install Git and Python 3.11 or newer, then clone the repository. These checks and the local website use only the Python standard library. The project environment below keeps any later dependencies separate from your other projects.
quickstart_preview: The smoke check prints a JSON report with status passed. Keep the server running and open the local project site below; Ctrl+C stops the server.
quickstart_python: The remaining commands use python from the activated macOS/Linux environment. On Windows, replace python with .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe. If you downloaded a ZIP instead of cloning, open its extracted repository folder and start with the environment commands.
quickstart_gpu: To prepare real model inputs or run prediction, supply the product data, model snapshot and checkpoints locally. Install the pinned neural dependencies in a separate project environment; the documented CUDA setup was checked on Windows 11 with an RTX 3060.
